parole.significato: accent (distinctive manner of pronouncing a language associated with a particular region, social group, etc.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French accent, from Latin accentus.

parole.testo: Borrowed from French accentuer, from Latin accentus. Compare Belarusian акцэнтава́ць (akcentavácʹ), Polish akcentować, Russian акценти́ровать (akcentírovatʹ). By surface analysis, акце́нт (akcént) + -ува́ти (-uváty).

parole.significato: alameda, allée, alley (walk or passage in a garden or park, bordered by rows of trees or bushes)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French allée. Compare Russian алле́я (alléja), Belarusian але́я (aljéja), Polish aleja.

parole.significato: album (a book specially designed to keep photographs, stamps, or autographs)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French album, from Latin album.

parole.significato: artist, performer (a practitioner of performing arts)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French artiste.

parole.significato: ball (formal or extravagant party or dance)

parole.significato: balance (list accounting for the debits on one side, and for the credits on the other)

parole.significato: lady (a woman of breeding or higher class, a woman of authority)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French dame (seemingly via Russian да́ма (dáma) and Polish dama, and via German Dame in the 'queen' playing card sense), from Latin domina (“lady”).

parole.significato: gesture (communicative motion of the limbs or body)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French geste, from Latin gestus.

parole.testo: Borrowed from French croissant.
